title: RBAC v2 Permission Workshop Notes (working)
content:
Doc purpose
- Working notes from cross-functional workshops to (a) enumerate candidate sensitive actions and map them to permissions, (b) pressure-test scope semantics (org vs project vs environment vs cluster), (c) capture disagreements/trade-offs.
- Not a final catalog. Expect contradictions + TODOs.

Workshops captured here
1) 2025-01-28 (90m) “Permission inventory kick-off”
   Attendees: Naomi, Marcus, Jordan, Amara, Ethan, Kaitlyn
2) 2025-02-06 (60m) “Scopes + control plane actions deep dive”
   Attendees: Naomi, Ethan, Ines, Diego, Jordan, Marcus
3) 2025-02-14 (75m) “Console/admin UX + denied messaging”
   Attendees: Naomi, Chloe, Tessa, Felix (partial), Marcus, Kaitlyn
4) 2025-02-26 (60m) “Private + Dedicated operational actions”
   Attendees: Vivek, Colin (partial), Diego, Ethan, Marcus, Naomi
5) 2025-03-19 (45m) “Audit export + SIEM + evidence expectations”
   Attendees: Kevin, Olga, Daniel (partial), Marcus, Naomi


Shared vocabulary (rough)
- Subject: user, service account, API key, automation token (Private installer?), support operator (internal)
- Action: permission string (e.g., org.user.invite)
- Resource: org, project, environment, deployment/cluster, api_key, secret, model_version, routing_policy, audit_log
- Scope: the boundary at which a role binding applies (org-level binding vs project binding vs env binding vs cluster binding)

Sensitivity tiers (draft; used for prioritization + extra audit requirements)
- Tier 0 (read-only / low risk): view metadata, list resources, view dashboards
- Tier 1 (moderate): create non-security resources, modify non-prod settings, manage prompts/evals (if applicable)
- Tier 2 (high): changes affecting traffic/routing, model pinning/rollouts, key creation/rotation, retention/residency settings
- Tier 3 (critical): org-level role changes, break-glass elevation, audit log export, secrets/KMS config, private deployment bootstrap/admin actions

Notes: tier is NOT policy, it’s classification to guide (a) default roles, (b) enforcement test coverage, (c) audit logging richness.


Permission naming (notes only; see ADR-014 for eventual decision)
- Proposed structure (Jordan + Marcus): <product_area>.<resource>.<verb>[.<qualifier>]  (e.g., console.role_binding.create, org.user.deactivate)
- Must be stable + versionable; deprecation policy needed (don’t churn strings)
- Debate: include scope in the string vs derive from resource? (strong preference: don’t embed scope in the permission name; scope belongs in the binding/resource)
- Debate: namespacing “hosted/dedicated/private” in the permission name vs separate applicability metadata. Outcome: prefer applicability metadata (same permission can be meaningful in multiple deployment modes).


Candidate sensitive actions (by product area)

A) Identity / Org admin / Membership
(Owner: control plane + console)
- Invite user to org
  - Tier: 2
  - Notes: invites can be used to expand access; should be controlled separately from “create project”
- Remove user from org
  - Tier: 2
- Deactivate user / lock account
  - Tier: 2
- Manage SSO settings (SAML/OIDC config), domain verification, SCIM
  - Tier: 3
  - Open question: do we split “view SSO settings” vs “edit SSO settings”?
- Manage org metadata (name, allowed domains, support contact)
  - Tier: 1
- Create / delete project
  - Tier: 2
  - Scope question: is project a hard boundary or just an organizing unit? If boundary, we must ensure all resources attach.

B) Roles / Role bindings / Permission management (core RBAC surface)
(Owner: Jordan + Chloe)
- Create custom role
  - Tier: 3 (because privilege crafting)
- Edit custom role (add/remove permissions)
  - Tier: 3
- Delete custom role
  - Tier: 3
- Assign role binding to user/group/service account
  - Tier: 3
- Revoke role binding
  - Tier: 3
- View role + permission viewer (including effective permissions)
  - Tier: 1 (but can leak internal details? see denial reason exposure discussion)
- View “who has access to X”
  - Tier: 1–2 depending on the resource (auditors want this)
- Break-glass: grant time-bound super-admin
  - Tier: 3

C) API keys / tokens / authn credentials
(Owner: gateway + control plane)
- Create API key
  - Tier: 2
  - Should be scoped to project and/or environment? (today: org-wide-ish; we need to decide)
- Rotate API key
  - Tier: 2
- Revoke API key
  - Tier: 2
- View API key metadata (last used, created by, name)
  - Tier: 1
- View API key secret value
  - Tier: 3 (strong recommendation: never re-display; only show at creation time)
- Manage service accounts (create/deactivate)
  - Tier: 2
  - Disagreement: treat service accounts like users (org.user.*) or a separate namespace (org.service_account.*)

D) Routing policies / traffic management / rollouts
(Owner: control plane + runtime ops)
- Create/edit routing policy (e.g., route A/B, region selection, fallback model)
  - Tier: 2
  - Critical for availability + cost control
- Enable/disable fallback policy
  - Tier: 2
- Modify traffic split / canary parameters
  - Tier: 2
- Pin model version for a route
  - Tier: 2
- Rollback route to previous model
  - Tier: 2
- Pause/resume routing
  - Tier: 2
- Emergency “route to safe model” action
  - Tier: 3? (availability critical; could be abused)
  - Discussion: should “emergency reroute” be separate from normal routing edit, to reduce blast radius?

E) Model catalog / model onboarding (customer-facing model availability)
(Owner: platform; mostly internal, but Private has “allowed models” concept)
- Configure allowed models for an org/project/environment
  - Tier: 2
- Add custom model endpoint (BYOM) / register private model artifact
  - Tier: 3 (depends on ability to exfiltrate data / run arbitrary code?)
- Change quantization profile / performance settings
  - Tier: 2
  - Debate: treat as “deployment operation” vs “model management”

F) Secrets / KMS / data protection settings
(Owner: Private deployments + security)
- Configure KMS key / HSM integration
  - Tier: 3
- Rotate encryption keys (where supported)
  - Tier: 3
- Configure secrets provider (Vault, KMS) in Private
  - Tier: 3
- Manage webhook signing secrets / integrations secrets
  - Tier: 3

G) Audit logs / compliance exports
(Owner: Kevin + logging)
- View audit logs
  - Tier: 1–2 (depending on content; may contain sensitive resource names)
- Export audit logs (download, SIEM push)
  - Tier: 3
- Configure audit log retention period
  - Tier: 3 (regulatory impact)
- Configure audit export destination (SIEM endpoint, token)
  - Tier: 3
- Redaction settings for logs (if any)
  - Tier: 2–3

H) Data retention / residency / privacy settings
(Owner: security + infra)
- Configure data retention for prompts/outputs
  - Tier: 3
- Configure data residency region constraints
  - Tier: 3
- Enable “no logging” or “restricted logging” mode
  - Tier: 3

I) Console admin tooling / support operations
(Owner: console + security)
- Impersonation / “support access” to customer org
  - Tier: 3 (internal-only)
  - Strong preference: controlled via separate internal system + break-glass; not a normal customer permission
- View customer org config (internal)
  - Tier: 2
- Apply account-level overrides (internal feature flags, throttling)
  - Tier: 3

J) Dedicated capacity + Private deployment operations
(Owner: Vivek + platform)
- Dedicated: change autoscaling settings / min-max capacity
  - Tier: 2
- Dedicated: attach/detach customer to a dedicated pool
  - Tier: 3 (availability + data isolation)
- Private: install/upgrade Redwood components
  - Tier: 3
- Private: bootstrap initial admin binding (“first admin”)
  - Tier: 3
- Private: configure cluster-level settings (ingress, TLS, allowed egress)
  - Tier: 3
- Private: rotate cluster credentials / certs
  - Tier: 3
- Private: enable/disable admin API endpoints
  - Tier: 3

K) Billing / quotas / usage limits
(Owner: product/ops)
- Set org spending limit / budget alerts
  - Tier: 2
- Modify quotas / rate limits
  - Tier: 2
  - Debate: is quota editing a security permission (DoS potential) vs billing/ops?
- View invoices / payment methods
  - Tier: 2
  - Likely separate “Billing Admin” role


Open questions (scope model)

1) What exactly is a “project” in RBAC v2?
- Option A: project is a true security boundary; most resources attach to project; roles bind at project scope
  - Pros: least-privilege; matches how enterprise customers think
  - Cons: migration complexity; many current resources are org-scoped
- Option B: project is mostly organizational; security boundary is org and/or environment
  - Pros: easier migration
  - Cons: less least-privilege; customers will ask for project separation anyway
- Notes: PM-661 to clarify. Need decision before we freeze permission/resource mapping.

2) Environments (prod/stage/dev): first-class scope or just tag?
- Strong asks from regulated customers: separate prod admin vs non-prod admin
- If environment is a binding scope, we must ensure every write action can be tied to an env (routing policy edits, model pinning, retention settings)
- Question: do we allow “org-level retention policy” that applies to all envs, or require explicit per-env config?

3) Private: what is “cluster scope” vs “environment scope”?
- Private deployments have literal clusters + namespaces (k8s). Customers may run multiple clusters per org.
- Potential model: scope types include org, project, environment, cluster.
- Concern (Jordan): too many scope types => policy evaluator + UI complexity.
- Counterpoint (Vivek): Private customers will demand separation of duties across clusters.

4) Are routing policies scoped to project or environment?
- Most intuitive: env (prod vs staging have different traffic)
- But some customers want shared routing templates across envs
- Possible compromise: routing policy resources are env-scoped; templates are org-scoped read-only

5) API keys: should keys be project-scoped? env-scoped? both?
- Today: keys often behave like org-level with optional restrictions.
- Proposal: create keys at project scope; optionally constrain to env. Don’t allow org-wide “god keys” by default.
- Migration: will break people who have one key for everything unless we do compatibility mapping.


Disagreements / trade-offs captured

A) Where to enforce authorization? Gateway vs service
- Amara: gateway should be deny-by-default to prevent accidental bypass; standard middleware is leverage
- Ethan: service must re-check for internal calls / non-gateway entry points; gateway-only is insufficient
- Jordan: “belt + suspenders” but avoid duplicate eval costs; need shared library + consistent context
- Tentative: gateway enforces for external requests; services enforce for any sensitive actions and for internal RPC boundaries; evaluation cached safely (see ENG notes).

B) Centralized policy evaluation service vs embedded library
- Performance vs operability debate (see ADR-015 thread)
- Concern: centralized service becomes critical path + outage multiplier
- Concern: embedded means multiple languages/services diverge
- Tentative direction (as of 2/06): embedded evaluator client with local cache, backed by policy bundle versioning; option to call central service for debugging only.

C) Denial reason exposure (“why was I denied?”)
- Tessa: users need actionable info; otherwise support load spikes
- Marcus: do not leak which permissions exist for sensitive internal-only actions; denial reasons should be sanitized
- Proposed compromise:
  - Default user-facing message: “You don’t have permission to perform this action.”
  - Admin-debug mode (or header): include reason code + required permission + scope mismatch details
  - Audit log always has full reason codes for forensics

D) Role templates vs custom roles for enterprise
- Naomi: templates are necessary to get customers started + reduce misconfiguration
- Jordan: custom roles are required; templates alone won’t satisfy least-privilege
- Decision-ish: ship templates + allow custom roles; but gate role creation/edit behind high-tier permission (Tier 3).

E) Scope explosion vs least-privilege
- Marcus/Olga: regulated customers will ask for separation of duties (Security Admin vs Deployment Operator vs Auditor)
- Platform concern: if we add org/project/env/cluster all at once, UX becomes too complex
- Proposal: phase scopes:
  - Phase 1: org + project + environment (if we can keep env simple)
  - Phase 2: cluster scope (Private) once Private installer + Console can support it cleanly


“Candidate permission” sketch (non-final strings)
(These are examples to sanity-check granularity; do not treat as final catalog.)
- org.user.invite
- org.user.remove
- org.sso.configure
- org.role.create
- org.role.update
- org.role_binding.create
- org.role_binding.delete
- project.api_key.create
- project.api_key.rotate
- project.api_key.revoke
- env.routing_policy.update
- env.routing_policy.rollback
- env.model_pin.update
- org.audit_log.view
- org.audit_log.export
- org.retention_policy.update
- private.cluster.upgrade
- private.cluster.bootstrap_admin

Note: need consistent verbs list (create/update/delete/view/export/rotate/assign/revoke/enable/disable). Jordan to propose a canonical verb set.


Gaps / “things we forgot last time” list
- Token-level cost dashboards: do we consider access to cost breakdown sensitive? (could reveal usage patterns)
- Export usage analytics (billing/telemetry) to CSV
- Webhooks: create/edit/delete webhooks (exfiltration vector)
- Prompt set / eval management (Optimize): who can upload customer prompts (PII risk)
- Data deletion requests (GDPR/DSAR style) if supported in Console
- Incident response actions (temporary blocks, forced key rotations) — internal-only but need to be represented in permissions for auditability


Action items (as of last edit 2025-03-21)
- Naomi: align with PM-661 on whether environment is first-class scope for v2 MVP; write a 1-pager recommendation + migration implications (ETA 3/25)
- Marcus: propose final tier definitions + which tiers require enhanced audit log fields + mandatory E2E tests (ETA 3/27)
- Jordan: propose canonical verb list + draft 30–50 core permissions for “critical path” endpoints to seed registry (ties to PR-28134) (ETA 3/28)
- Amara: list all gateway routes that mutate security-relevant resources; flag any that bypass gateway (streaming included) (ETA 3/26)
- Ethan + Ines: map control-plane endpoints to (resource type, scope type) and call out any endpoints with ambiguous scope (ETA 3/29)
- Chloe + Tessa: define Console MVP workflows (role bindings, templates, permission viewer, denied UX) and which require admin-debug view (DES-927 alignment) (ETA 4/02)
- Kevin: confirm SIEM export expectations for authz decision logging fields + what customers consider “minimum viable evidence” (ETA 3/31)


Loose references / breadcrumbs
- See Slack threads linked above for exact arguments on naming + enforcement.
- Related pain observed in pilots: customers hitting 403s on key rotation + routing policy edits after role migration (support threads + Jira tickets; not pasted here).
- Reminder: include Dedicated + Private semantics from day 1 even if UI phases them later; otherwise we’ll fork permissions.

End of notes (for now).
